correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the exact unique decomposition recurrence, bounded-gap automaton and its transfer generating function, strict positive power of period matrix for every f, analytic Perron quasi-power, Markov reward variance via a Poisson-equation martingale decomposition, and exact consecutive-interval reduction. All-zero and positive-reward return loops prohibit zero asymptotic variance. Standalone executable exhaustively cross-checks 507 finite histograms and fixed finite primitivity witnesses; finite tests are not claimed to prove infinite asymptotics.

originality.rationale: Question (3) of Demontigny et al. 2013 explicitly asks the universality proved here. Comparisons with broader automata and adjacent number-theory work identified no literally stated or directly dominating all-periodic f theorem. Bertoni et al. (2003) gives the main general central-limit framework but its primitive one-letter matrix hypothesis does not directly hold for the periodic phase-augmented digit automaton; the period-block matrix has multivalued block rewards and the uniform positivity check is supplied anew. An alternate encoding might reduce the result to earlier regular-language machinery, so novelty is not independently certified.
residual_risks: A re-encoding under an existing broad regular-language or Markov additive central-limit theorem could make the all-periodic result an unstated corollary; Bertoni et al. is the strongest comparison checked.

value.rationale: Closes precisely the full periodic-case Gaussian open Question 5(3) from the 2013 primary number-theory paper, including variable gap patterns that need not be within a fixed b-bin structure. Supplies an effectively computable finite transfer-matrix formula and proves strictly positive linear variance for all fixed periodic patterns, making the limit nondegenerate. This structural universal result is not a small numeric increment or unmotivated slice.
